checks.subject: Owner-only and release boundaries
checks.proof: Readiness is held until all G01-G24 gates pass. Login, publication, destination/public history, tag/release, visibility, hosted-publisher configuration and faulty-release registry mutations remain owner actions. No authorization is inferred from these instructions.

checks.subject: Exact reviewed handoff and package inputs
checks.proof: The first shell block pins Node/npm, enters the reviewed public checkout, requires exact handoff HEAD and clean Git state, checks implementation ancestry and unchanged package/build inputs, then verifies package and final public source SHA-256. It inspects the package manifest and performs only a dry-run before later authority steps.

checks.subject: Final identity without a self-hash cycle
checks.proof: The final handoff commit and final public source digest are delivered in a separate manifest outside the source archive it hashes. The tested implementation/archive identities remain separate. The final manifest also binds refs, reviewed docs/media, scans, advisory triage and gate dispositions. Its own digest is not embedded inside itself.

checks.subject: Destination privacy and exact ref push
checks.proof: The empty-or-reviewed destination requirement precedes the push. Existing refs and hosted PR/release/Actions content remain part of the destination review. The push names only the approved handoff SHA and refs/heads/main, with --no-follow-tags. The guide stops on private destination content or non-fast-forward history and does not silently replace an existing remote.

checks.subject: npm authority and provenance routes
checks.proof: The interactive route requires account 2FA, login/whoami and explicit owner verification when the package exists. E404 is not authority or reservation. Existing 0.1.0 stops publication. The local route is explicitly without provenance. The hosted route requires a public matching repository, hosted runner permissions, exact rebuilt package equality, separately configured authority and owner approval. Trusted-publisher staging defaults, first-publication expiry, explicit publish action, separate dist-tag permission and first-stage placeholder are retained as current-source-backed policy from the accepted prereview and root refresh. No route is claimed configured.

checks.subject: Registry archive and separate name installation
checks.proof: A fresh cache and directory retrieve pinned-version metadata and archive. JavaScript asserts package name/version, approved SHA-256 and a matching SHA-512 SRI token before execution. A separate registry-name installation provides registry lock identity for audit signatures. The guide requires inspection of this package attestation source commit and workflow, rather than treating dependency signatures as package provenance.

checks.subject: Installed behavioral verification and public-app scope
checks.proof: Both invocations match actual two-argument script interfaces. installCandidate installs the supplied archive, hashes its bytes, imports installed schemas and calls its installed binary. The package smoke covers help/doctor/plan, successful and partial compare, browser-unavailable composition, encoder failure/recovery, WORKTREE and cleanup assertions. The public script runs navigation and validation three times each plus validation WORKTREE. Both save report.json with passed/failed and candidate.sha256, and set exit 1 on failure. Normal-speed inspection remains explicit. These are future post-publish actions, not newly executed evidence.

checks.subject: Prerequisites, sequencing and error handling
checks.proof: Node 24.22.2 and npm 11.12.1 are checked at entry. Browser installation and doctor appear in the review sequence. The post-publication section links the quickstart for browser/system prerequisites, states pnpm 11.9.0, and checks it before both workloads. The public fixture declares that pnpm version and uses only local workspace links in its frozen offline lock. set -eu and assertions stop digest, version, ancestry or command failures. Expected absent registry records require the stated inspection; network/auth errors stay unresolved. No script claim substitutes for platform or visual acceptance.

checks.proof: Reversing the privacy-paragraph relocation and pnpm prose/version check reproduces the integration record hashes. Reversing each of the nine prereview edits then reproduces both prereview document hashes exactly. This excludes any additional undocumented current document change.
